title: Landing tagline & modular inference playbook
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc collects a set of fresh homepage/landing and product page copy directions that emphasize a modular, composable inference story — not just "fast" or "cheap" but "compose the right inference for your product constraints." The goal: short hero hooks + 3–4 supporting subheads and microcopy variants for product pages (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private), and a simple test matrix.

Primary positioning claim (one line):
- Modular inference: pick the latency, cost, and control profile your feature needs — with one API surface.

Why this angle?
- Differentiator: many competitors pitch single promises (fast, inexpensive, or secure) — modularity reframes the problem as a composition problem developers already understand (picking CPU/GPU/quantization/cache policies like libraries).
- Customer pain: teams juggling tradeoffs across features (chat vs. search vs. agent tooling) want predictable economics and a single integration.
- Fits product: Redwood already supports Hosted / Dedicated / Private and runtime routing, so this is an honest claim with operational hooks.

Hero tagline variants (short, A/B friendly) — prioritized order for experiments:
A1 (developer-centric, explicit control): "One inference API. Compose latency, cost, and privacy."
A2 (value-first, metric hook): "Ship features faster — control latency and unit economics from one API."
A3 (ops-friendly, trust): "Predictable LLM inference — across hostings, hardware, and fallbacks."
A4 (compact & punchy): "Compose inference. Control outcomes."

Supporting one-liners (use under each hero for quick scannability):
- "Route by latency, cost, or compliance — automatically or with policy pins."
- "Verified performance profiles for popular open models and quantized variants."
- "Built-in caching, batching, and graceful fallbacks — fewer surprises in production."

Microcopy and product area lines (homepage tiles or product nav):
- Hosted API: "Fastest time-to-value with transparent performance and usage insights."
- Dedicated: "Reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput for business-critical features."
- Private: "Bring Redwood into your VPC or on-prem for isolated, auditable inference."
- Optimize add-on: "Automated batching, quant profiles, and cost recommendations tied to your real workloads."

Differentiation bullets (3–5 bullets under hero or on product page):
- "Unified API across deployments — same routes, same SDKs, fewer integration forks."
- "Decision controls: pin models, enforce region routing, or let adaptive routing optimize for cost."
- "Observability that maps to unit economics — token-level latency and cost breakdowns."
- "Runtime-first optimizations: continuous batching, prefix caching, and quant-aware kernels."

Competitor notes (brief, for internal use in copy commentary):
- Comp A (managed LLM endpoints): emphasizes simplicity but hides per-token economics and has limited private deployment options. Use: call out "transparent unit economics" and "private deploys" in GTM copy.
- Comp B (self-hosted runtime): sells control and lower TCO but high ops overhead. Use: highlight "same API without building the stack" and "dedicated capacity contracts".
- Comp C (cloud vendor LLM): broad integrations and scale, weaker story on model rollback/fallback and model catalog curation. Use: emphasize curated performance profiles and automatic fallbacks in product copy.

Product page wire copy (structured for 3 panels):
Panel 1: What it is — one short paragraph (40–60 words):
"Redwood Inference is a modular runtime for LLM-powered features. Connect once, then choose how requests are served: low-latency variants for chat, cost-optimized routes for embeddings, and private deployments for regulated data — all from the same API and SDKs."

Panel 2: How it works — bulleted micro-explanations:
- "Smart routing: policies route requests by latency, cost, region, or customer tier."
- "Runtime optimizations: batching, KV caching, and model-variant kernels reduce cost without surprise latency spikes."
- "Safety & controls: pin versions, audit calls, and integrate KMS for key management."

Panel 3: Proof points & social/metrics (short):
- "Verified 50–70% cost reductions on long-tail embeddings workloads with caching and batching."
- "99.95% SLA for dedicated capacity customers (monthly uptime)."
- "Case study: SearchX reduced 95th percentile latency by 40% after switching to Redwood routing and quantized variants."

Headline-to-CTA microflows (3 quick sequences):
1) Hero A1 -> CTA "Try the API" -> Landing: sign up + quickstart that preconfigures a chat sample with low-latency route.
2) Hero A2 -> CTA "Calculate savings" -> Landing: simple unit economics calculator that compares baseline per-token cost vs. Redwood suggestions.
3) Hero A3 -> CTA "Request a demo" -> Private/Dedicated page for enterprise flow.

Measurement plan / test matrix (what to measure in first 6 weeks):
- Primary metric: signup-to-API-key activation conversion (tracking per hero variant).
- Secondary metrics: time to first call, percent of teams pinning model/version, demo request rate for Private.
- Qualitative: developer feedback on "clarity of tradeoff" from user interviews.

Copy dos and don'ts (quick guardrails):
Do:
- Use “compose” language — it signals modularity and developer control.
- Quantify where possible (% savings, latency gains, SLA numbers).
- Keep hero lines <= 6–7 words for mobile/scannability.

Don't:
- Velcro on vague promises like "best" or "fastest" without context.
- Overload hero with technical details (put specifics in support panels).

Risks and unresolved decisions (for PM/Product):
- How explicit should we be about quantization/accuracy tradeoffs on product pages? Need legal/security review for claims about accuracy regressions.
- Unit econ calculator inputs: need a short spec from Applied ML to estimate savings ranges for different workloads.
- Experiment length: recommend minimum 3 weeks per hero variant to collect signal on signup conversion.

Next steps / owner assignments:
- Draft A/B hero assets and localized microcopy (Owner: Marco Liu) — due 2026-02-20.
- Build a simple unit-econ calculator prototype for the landing page (Owner: Product-analytics) — sketch by 2026-03-01.
- Coordinate a small dev-user panel to validate "compose" language (Owner: Sofia Ramirez) — recruit by 2026-02-25.

Appendix — short alternate phrasing bank (one-line flairs for component pages):
- "Tune inference like a dependency — swap models, pins, and routes without code rewrites."
- "Keep control: per-route SLAs, region pins, and automatic fallbacks."
- "Lower unit cost without rebuilding your infra."
- "One SDK. Multiple runtimes. Predictable outcomes."

Notes/edits log:
- 2025-10-12 initial sketch (Aisha)
- 2025-11-14 added competitor callouts (Marco)
- 2026-01-10 inserted measurement plan and CTA flows (Sofia)
- 2026-02-08 editorial pass and status -> in_review (Aisha)

Use this doc as the canonical starting brief for next-steps in creative and engineering. Keep iterations in this Drive doc, then move final variants into the homepage experiment repo when approved.
